item.title: Probabilistically Exact Convexification of Mixed-Integer Quadratic Optimization with Indicators
item.description: We study the convexification of mixed-integer quadratic optimization with indicator variables. The problem remains NP-hard even when the quadratic matrix has bandwidth two, posing a fundamental obstacle to tractable exact convexification. To overcome this challenge in realistic settings, we introduce probabilistically exact (inner) convexification, a framework that relaxes the requirement of exactness for every objective ... item.title: Computing the Minimum Covariance Determinant
item.description: The minimum covariance determinant (MCD) problem selects a fixed-cardinality subset of data points to minimize its sample covariance determinant. We develop approximation and exact algorithms and apply them to prediction residuals, using the mean and covariance of the selected subset to define ellipsoidal conformal regions. For rational data, quadratic-form selection yields a deterministic approximation scheme ... Read more

Unlike traditional chatbots, GAI chatbots generate responses dynamically rather than relying on pre-programmed replies, enabling more natural and interactive engagement. The inconsistency of metadata across sources is a persistent problem for large-scale music research. The variety of approaches to documenting even basic elements such as artists’ names and work titles makes it difficult to aggregate data across different sources. item.description: The classical traffic assignment problem determines the equilibrium flows on a congested network with many infinitesimal users who choose paths to minimize their own travel times. item.description: Many integer programs assign indivisible items to capacitated resources, each contributing a knapsack constraint with a setup variable. We study linear combinatorial optimization problems where uncertain disruptions may affect the components (i.e., coefficients) of the objective function. Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. item.description:
José A. Capitán, Alberto Megías, Cristina Sardón
We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. item.description:
Till Preuster, Karl Worthmann, Lars Grüne, Manuel Schaller
Cost controllability, relating controllability and a performance measure like the stage cost in model predictive control (MPC), is a key tool in the stability and suboptimality analysis of closed-loop systems. item.description:
Xiao Ling
Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. By stating optimality conditions for weighted sum scalarizations, we derive parametric equations for Pareto critical points, parameterized by the weights. Yuming Bao, Yancheng Wu, Dongdong Ge, Yinyu Ye
Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. item.description:
Daniel Cortild, Coralia Cartis
Worst-case complexity bounds often fail to reflect the practical performance of optimization algorithms, while average-case complexity heavily relies on the distribution of the input. In this work, we develop a smoothed-analysis framework for classical continuous optimization algorithms by studying their behaviour on random perturbations of arbitrary functions. Ziming Wang, Kun Huang, Karl Henrik Johansson, Shi Pu
In this paper, we study the convergence of Federated Averaging (FedAvg) with partial participation under a general variance condition. In each communication round, the server samples $S$ of the $n$ clients uniformly at random without replacement. item.description:
Jonas Westin
National freight transport models usually treat prices and service provision as exogenous. This paper models both as outcomes of strategic interaction among operators of scheduled, loop-based freight services. It compares oligopolistic competition, monopoly, Ramsey pricing with service-level or system-wide cost recovery, and welfare-maximising planning. item.title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
item.description:
Stefan Kuhlmann, Timm Oertel, Nicola Wengiel
The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. item.description:

item.description:
Reyajul Hasan Leon, Ali Devran Kara
We study discrete-time stochastic control problems where the noise driving the state dynamics is a stationary infinite-order chain rather than an i.i.d. sequence.
